system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## REVIEW OF SELLER DOCUMENTS AGAINST BUYER PLAYBOOK
**Project Kestrel | Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer) | Harbourglass Ventures (Seller)**

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Seller’s updated SPA and Disclosure Letter **depart materially from the playbook on every core protection**. The Seller has:
- adopted the **fallback cap (20% / $4.8M)** and **fallback time limit (18 months)** without the required principal approval;
- collapsed **fundamental/title warranties** into the general regime;
- **eliminated the fraud carve-out** entirely;
- imposed **whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure**;
- inserted a **blanket “discoverable” buyer-knowledge bar**;
- reduced **Bluefen** to reasonable endeavours + consent-on-delivery;
- kicked **Riverlark** repayment and security release to post-completion with no irrevocable undertaking;
- **silently excluded** the $420k employee bonuses (+ on-costs) from the funds flow;
- refused to broaden the **Ironquay** indemnity;
- treated **Tax/IP** as “settled” under the general regime; and
- offered **only the internal share register** for title.

**Bottom line:** This draft is not a “fair and balanced package”—it is a systematic rollback of the Buyer’s baseline protections. Every item below requires a hard mark-up; several are walk-away issues if not corrected.

---

## 1. GENERAL WARRANTY CAP — FALLBACK USED WITHOUT AUTHORITY
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| 25% / $6M starting; 20% / $4.8M **only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given)** | Clause 12.1: 20% / $4.8M | **Material.** The Seller has unilaterally taken the conditional fallback as its opening bid. No principal approval exists. We must reinstate 25% / $6M as the opening position and only concede 20% with written authority. |

## 2. THRESHOLDS — 5× WIDER THAN PLAYBOOK
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis $5k; basket $50k (first-dollar recovery once exceeded) | Clause 12.2: De minimis $25k; basket $250k (excess-only recovery) | **Material.** Seller’s thresholds are 5× higher on both legs and convert the basket to “excess only,” effectively gifting the Seller the first $250k of aggregate liability. Push back to playbook numbers and first-dollar recovery. |

## 3. GENERAL CLAIMS PERIOD — FALLBACK USED WITHOUT AUTHORITY
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| 24 months; 18 months **only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given)** | Clause 12.3/13: 18 months | **Material.** Same pattern as the cap: the conditional fallback is presented as the opening position. Reinstate 24 months. |

## 4. FUNDAMENTAL / TITLE WARRANTIES — COLLAPSED INTO GENERAL REGIME
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | “Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.” | **Critical / Walk-away.** This eliminates the separate fundamental-warranty regime entirely. Title, capacity, authority, and ownership claims would be subject to the $4.8M cap, 18-month limit, $250k basket, and buyer-knowledge bar. **Must be rejected outright.** |

## 5. FRAUD / WILFUL CONCEALMENT / DELIBERATE MISCONDUCT — NO CARVE-OUT
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance; non-waivable | Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5: “limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**.” | **Critical / Walk-away.** The Seller expressly includes fraud in the general limitations. This is unenforceable as a matter of public policy in NSW, but the clause as drafted creates interpretation risk and must be redlined to insert the full carve-out. |

## 6. DISCLOSURE — WHOLE DATA ROOM + PUBLIC REGISTERS
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure | Disclosure Letter 1.1: “every fact…in the indexed electronic data room”; 1.2: “Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records.” | **Material.** This is the exact “general disclosure” the playbook forbids. It shifts the burden to the Buyer to find needles in the haystack. Require **specific, paragraph-by-paragraph disclosure** tied to each warranty; delete general disclosure provisions. |

## 7. BUYER KNOWLEDGE — BLANKET “DISCOVERABLE” BAR
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier = named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity | Clause 8.3: “no claim…of which the Buyer **or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records**.” | **Material.** “Discoverable” is an objective constructive-knowledge standard far broader than actual knowledge. It also applies to title, capacity, and fraud (contrary to playbook). Delete clause 8.3 entirely; if a knowledge qualifier is needed, limit to **actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals** after reasonable enquiry, and carve out title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities. |

## 8. BLUEFEN CONSENT — REASONABLE ENDEAVOURS + CONSENT-ON-DELIVERY
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Effective consent **AND evidence conditions satisfied** before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient | Clause 3/6.3: “Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty’s written consent.” | **Material.** Bluefen = ~30% revenue ($3.6M FY26). The Seller has **not** delivered final written consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied (Disclosure 2). Reasonable endeavours + consent-on-delivery leaves the Buyer exposed to a failed condition post-completion. Require: (a) executed consent **before** Completion; (b) evidence all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied; (c) condition precedent, not reasonable endeavours. |

## 9. RIVERLARK FACILITY — POST-COMPLETION RELEASE ONLY
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval | Clause 2/7: “release to be provided **following Completion**.” Disclosure 3: facility **not repaid**, no final discharge included. | **Material.** $3.2M debt on a debt-free/cash-free deal. Kicking repayment and security release to post-completion with no irrevocable undertaking (and no principal approval) leaves the Buyer exposed to lingering security interests and enforcement risk. Require: (a) full payout **from Completion funds**; (b) executed discharges/releases **at Completion**; (c) if any post-completion step is unavoidable, irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost written approval. |

## 10. EMPLOYEE BONUSES (DD-005) — SILENTLY EXCLUDED FROM FUNDS FLOW
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| $420k + triggered on-costs = specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude | “DD-005 closing bonuses…are a matter for the Seller and are **not separately itemised in the funds flow**.” Disclosure 5: on-costs (payroll tax, super) **not addressed**. | **Material.** The Seller treats $420k (+ on-costs) as its internal problem but does not fund it in the funds flow. On a debt-free/cash-free basis, this liability will reduce the cash at Completion unless expressly carved out. Require: (a) specific line item in funds flow for $420k + on-costs; (b) Seller funds or price adjustment; (c) disclosure of on-cost quantum. |

## 11. IRONQUAY IP INDEMNITY — NARROW SCOPE RETAINED
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| Broaden narrow indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; $180k not independently verified | Clause 11.1: “existing indemnity…limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.” Disclosure 4: $180k open; **no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment in data room**. | **Material.** The Seller refuses to broaden the indemnity despite unverified payment status and missing assignment. The playbook requires a broader indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure. Mark up to expand scope (breach of IP warranty, third-party claims, defence costs) and keep
=== END ADVICE ===
